title: Oscar and the Salt
premise: Isandro Hartwell, a mercenary whose god fell silent a decade ago, sells outlawed charms in the salt-locked city of Verrane until a child named Oscar arrives at his door speaking the dead tongue of Ilvaren, a country erased from maps and memory. The boy's words are slowly unmaking the erasure itself, and every hour he speaks, the vanished nation bleeds back into the world — dragging its wars, its debts, and its hungry dead with it. Hunted by the Salt Wardens who enforce the forgetting and betrayed by the order that once swore him to the silent god, Isandro discovers Oscar is the last heir of Ilvaren, and that the door out of the country exists only where someone remembers it whole. In the end Isandro must choose between sealing the door forever to save the city he loves and speaking the country back into being at the cost of his own name, which the old magic demands as payment; he speaks it, loses himself to the erasure, and Oscar carries both their memories through into a world remade.
about_author: Odile Okafor is a former archivist who spent six years cataloguing confiscated grimoires before turning to fiction. She writes from a coastal town whose name she declines to confirm, and claims her stories are all translations of books that no longer exist.

chapters.title: The Price of Small Wonders
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. In the salt-fogged market of Verrane, Isandro sells a luck-charm to a grieving widow, hiding how weak his magic has become since his god went silent. A Warden raid nearly catches him; an old debt is called in. Emotional beat: weary pragmatism masking grief for a faith that abandoned him.

chapters.title: A Knock in Dead Tongues
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. On a storm night, a mud-caked child of eight or nine appears at his door speaking a language Isandro shouldn't understand but does — the liturgical tongue of Ilvaren, the country history says never existed. The boy knows Isandro's true name. Emotional beat: dread and reluctant wonder.

chapters.title: What the Maps Refuse
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Researching in a smuggler's archive, Isandro finds maps with a salt-shaped hole where Ilvaren should be, and learns the boy's speech is physically erasing ink around them. The first Warden tracker arrives asking about 'unlicensed sound.' Emotional beat: the thrill of forbidden knowledge curdling into fear.

chapters.title: Oscar
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The boy remembers another life: a mother singing this language, a palace of white stone, soldiers made of brine. He doesn't know why he was sent to Isandro specifically, only that a voice told him 'the sworn one will know the door.' Emotional beat: loneliness of carrying memories no adult believes.

chapters.title: The Order of the Quiet Bell
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. His former commander, Serah Voss, finds him and reveals the god didn't die — it was silenced deliberately when the orders helped erase Ilvaren, trading their divinity for amnesty. She offers protection if he surrenders the boy. Emotional beat: betrayal reframing ten years of abandonment.

chapters.title: Salt on the Threshold
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Warden raid on Isandro's shop; he escapes with Oscar through a charm-door that only works because Oscar's words briefly remember a road that no longer exists. First proof the boy can open ways. Emotional beat: fugitive adrenaline, first real bond forming.

chapters.title: The Road That Remembers Us
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Traveling the remembered road, Isandro and Oscar pass villages where people hum songs they've never learned and weep without knowing why. Isandro teaches Oscar survival; Oscar teaches Isandro prayers his own god once answered. Emotional beat: found-family tenderness under pursuit.

chapters.title: Serah's Bargain
chapters.summary: Serah's POV. Pressured by the Wardens' Grand Auditor, Serah traces Isandro while wrestling with her own complicity in the silencing. Flashback to the night the gods went quiet and what she saw in the salt. Emotional beat: loyalty to an institution rotting from within.

chapters.title: The Hungry Congregation
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The returning memory of Ilvaren raises its dead as salt-effigies who seek Oscar, not to harm him but to serve him — and their devotion is devouring the living land around them. Isandro realizes the restoration is killing the present to resurrect the past. Emotional beat: horror at unintended consequences.

chapters.title: Where the God Went
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Guided by the effigies, Oscar reaches a drowned chapel and hears the silent god — not dead but imprisoned inside the erasure, whispering fragments. It calls Oscar 'heir' and Isandro 'debtor.' Emotional beat: awe and terror of touching something vast and wounded.

chapters.title: Confessions at the Fireline
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Cornered by Wardens, Isandro tells Oscar the truth: he was one of the mercenaries who helped burn Ilvaren's border-stones; his silence-god was his penance. Oscar's trust shatters. Emotional beat: guilt confessed too late, love tested against truth.

chapters.title: The Auditor's Cage
chapters.summary: Serah's POV. Oscar is captured; Isandro escapes wounded. Serah interrogates the boy and discovers the Grand Auditor isn't preserving peace — he's consuming Ilvaren's returned magic to extend his own life. Emotional beat: disillusionment completing Serah's turn.

chapters.title: Debt of the Sworn
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Dying of Warden wounds, Isandro bargains with the imprisoned god: his name, his memory, his entire self as payment for one door opened. The god accepts. Emotional beat: grim resolve — choosing sacrifice over survival.

chapters.title: Rescue Written in Brine
chapters.summary: Serah's POV. Serah defects, freeing Oscar and smuggling him to Isandro, paying for it with her rank and nearly her life. She gives Isandro the Auditor's ledger proving the erasure was theft, not mercy. Emotional beat: redemption purchased at cost.

chapters.title: The Door Out of a Country
chapters.summary: Dual POV. At the drowned border-stone, Isandro begins the rite to open the way out — but the door leads nowhere unless someone remembers Ilvaren whole, and only Oscar's mind holds enough of it. The Auditor arrives with the full Warden host. Emotional beat: cornered hope.

chapters.title: The Grand Auditor's Truth
chapters.summary: Auditor's POV (first time). He reveals he was Ilvaren's royal archivist who engineered the erasure to escape a plague-wracked dying nation, and he will not let it return because its return means admitting what he destroyed. Emotional beat: villainy revealed as cowardice wearing duty's face.

chapters.title: Battle of the White Stone
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The salt-effigies rise to defend Oscar; Serah holds the Wardens' line; Isandro fights toward the stone as the Auditor unmakes the remembered road piece by piece. Oscar begins speaking the whole of Ilvaren aloud. Emotional beat: desperate, costly stand.

chapters.title: Everything Must Be Paid For
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The rite completes only as the god collects: Isandro's memories burn away chapter by chapter — his childhood, his service, his guilt, finally his name. He keeps speaking the closing words he no longer understands. Emotional beat: tragic transcendence.

chapters.title: Ilvaren, Spoken Whole
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The country returns — not conquering the present but settling over the salt like a tide, its people waking in new lives, its god freed and finally answering. The Auditor crumbles into ordinary salt. Oscar holds a man with no name who smiles at him anyway. Emotional beat: grief braided with miracle.

chapters.title: The Man Called Nothing
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The restored Ilvaren offers Oscar his inheritance: crown, palace, duty. He sees what the throne cost his mother's ghost-memory and hesitates. The nameless Isandro, content as a stranger, tends lamps in the chapel. Emotional beat: inheritance examined rather than assumed.

chapters.title: Two Names, One Door
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Oscar refuses the crown, instead founding a school of remembering so no country can be erased again; the god grants Isandro a new, small name — chosen, not owed. Serah becomes the school's first warden of a different kind. Emotional beat: quiet rebuilding after ruin.

chapters.title: Oscar and the Salt
chapters.summary: Years later, Oscar's POV. An adult Oscar walks the shore with the man called Isandro-now-named, teaching children the old tongue. The sea gives back small wonders freely now. He tells them the story of the door, the debt, and the man who paid it. Emotional beat: peace earned, memory kept sacred, love outlasting names.
